# valdo.yaml reference

<!-- Generated by `python -m valdo.easy.docgen` from valdo/easy/project.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

**For:** anyone editing `valdo.yaml`. **You need first:** a `valdo.yaml` written by `valdo init`
(see [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md)).

`valdo.yaml` is the one project file. `valdo init` writes it with a comment on every line;
this page lists every setting with its default and allowed values.

How the file is read:

- Unknown or misspelled keys are errors, with a suggestion (`advanced.train.epoch` -> did you
  mean `advanced.train.epochs`?). A typo never silently falls back to a default.
- Numbers written as text, such as `'1e-3'` (YAML reads `1e-3` without a dot as text), are
  converted, with a note.
- In paths, `~` and `$VARIABLES` are expanded. Relative paths are relative to the folder that
  holds `valdo.yaml`.
- A missing optional key takes the default below. `valdo init` writes every key, so the file
  is the single source of truth.
- Patterns (`models.per_dataset`, `phases.existing`, `validation.bound_models`) are either a
  path containing `{name}` (replaced by each dataset name), a folder, or a quoted glob. Files
  are matched to datasets by name.
- Column "upstream" names the field of the upstream stage config (`<workdir>/configs/<stage>.yaml`)
  that the setting fills.


## Part 1: your project

Where the data are, which models to use, where results go. Always look at these.

| setting | default | allowed values | meaning | upstream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | (none) | path or pattern; **required** | MTZ files: a folder, a glob pattern (in quotes) or a .txt file with one path per line |  |
| `models.apo` | `null` | path; or `null` | one apo model (PDB) for every dataset; also the fallback for datasets without their own model |  |
| `models.per_dataset` | `null` | path or pattern; or `null` | one model per dataset: a pattern with {name}, or a folder/glob whose file names contain the dataset name |  |
| `workdir` | `"valdo_run"` | path | all results go here (relative paths are relative to this file) |  |

## Part 2: detected by `valdo init`

Check these; change them only if init got something wrong.

| setting | default | allowed values | meaning | upstream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `columns.amplitude` | `"F-obs"` | text | observed structure-factor amplitude column (same name in every file) | `standardize.expcolumns` |
| `columns.sigma` | `"SIGF-obs"` | text | its standard-deviation column | `standardize.expcolumns` |
| `phases.source` | `"input_mtz"` | `input_mtz` / `refine` / `existing` | where map phases come from: input_mtz (map coefficients already in the data files), refine (refine every dataset), existing (your refined MTZs) |  |
| `phases.existing` | `null` | path or pattern; or `null` | source: existing -> your refined MTZs (pattern with {name}, folder or glob) |  |
| `phases.program` | `null` | `phenix` / `dimple`; or `null` | source: refine -> refinement program: phenix or dimple |  |
| `phases.columns.fwt` | `"2FOFCWT"` | text; or `null` | 2mFo-DFc amplitude column in the phase files (context maps) |  |
| `phases.columns.phwt` | `"PH2FOFCWT"` | text; or `null` | 2mFo-DFc phase column (phases for the VALDO difference maps) | `add_phases_and_blobs.phase_2FOFC_col_in` |
| `phases.columns.delfwt` | `"FOFCWT"` | text; or `null` | mFo-DFc amplitude column |  |
| `phases.columns.phdelwt` | `"PHFOFCWT"` | text; or `null` | mFo-DFc phase column | `add_phases_and_blobs.phase_FOFC_col_in` |
| `phases.rfree` | `null` | text; or `null` | R-free flag column in the phase files (null = none) | `add_phases_and_blobs.rfree_label_in` |
| `reindex` | `"auto"` | auto / true / false | auto \| true \| false. auto = only if the lattice allows alternative indexing (as upstream reindex decides) |  |
| `reference` | `"auto"` | text | reference dataset name, or auto = the first dataset (by ID) that passes the input checks |  |
| `focal_residue.seqid` | `null` | whole number; or `null` | residue number to exclude blobs around (PTP1B: 215 for Cys215); null = none | `tag_blobs.focal_seqid` |
| `focal_residue.radius` | `5.0` | number; >= 0 | exclusion radius in A | `tag_blobs.focal_radius` |
| `focal_residue.tag` | `"focal"` | text | name of the tag column in the blob tables (e.g. cys215) | `tag_blobs.focal_tag_name` |
| `validation.bound_models` | `null` | path or pattern; or `null` | optional: known ligand-bound models, for a descriptive check in the report | `tag_blobs.bound_models_folder` |
| `validation.ligand_resnames` | `["LIG"]` | list of text | ligand residue names in those models |  |
| `compute.ncpu` | `4` | whole number; >= 1 | worker processes for the parallel stages (use your batch job's slot count) | `<stage>.ncpu` |

## Part 3: advanced

Pre-filled with the settings validated on the PTP1B screen (upstream `_TEMPLATES` and `PTP1B_pipeline/configs`). Change them only if you know why.

| setting | default | allowed values | meaning | upstream |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `advanced.reindex.wcorr` | `true` | true / false | weighted per-resolution-shell CC (upstream template value; the schema fallback would be false) | `reindex.wcorr` |
| `advanced.reindex.cc_min_dif` | `0.2` | number; >= 0 | keep both indexing variants if their CCs differ by less than this | `reindex.cc_min_dif` |
| `advanced.scale.when_opt` | `"all"` | "all", "never" or a number in [0, 1] | "all", "never" or a number in [0, 1]: when to refine B/anisotropy numerically | `scale.when_opt` |
| `advanced.filter.max_rfree` | `0.45` | number; >= 0, <= 1 | drop datasets whose R-free after refinement is above this (phases.source: refine only) | `filter.max_rfree` |
| `advanced.filter.min_cc` | `0.55` | number; >= 0, <= 1 | drop datasets whose CC to the reference after scaling is below this (0 = off) | `filter.min_cc` |
| `advanced.train.latent_dim` | `7` | whole number; >= 1 | latent dimensions | `train.latent_dim` |
| `advanced.train.n_hidden_layers` | `[3, 6]` | list of whole numbers | [encoder, decoder] hidden layers | `train.n_hidden_layers` |
| `advanced.train.n_hidden_size` | `100` | whole number; >= 1 | units per hidden layer | `train.n_hidden_size` |
| `advanced.train.epochs` | `500` | whole number; >= 1 | training epochs | `train.epochs` |
| `advanced.train.train_fraction` | `0.8` | number; >= 0, <= 1 | fraction of datasets used for training (the rest validates); must be < 1 | `train.train_fraction` |
| `advanced.train.batch_size` | `100` | whole number; >= 1 | minibatch size | `train.batch_size` |
| `advanced.train.learning_rate` | `0.001` | number; >= 0 | Adam learning rate | `train.learning_rate` |
| `advanced.train.w_kl` | `1.0` | number; >= 0 | weight of the KL term | `train.w_kl` |
| `advanced.train.eps` | `0.02` | number; >= 0 | noise floor added to sigma(F) | `train.eps` |
| `advanced.train.stdof` | `128` | whole number; >= 1; or `null` | Student-t degrees of freedom of the loss; null = Gaussian | `train.stdof` |
| `advanced.train.include_errors` | `true` | true / false | use sigma(F) in the loss (must be true: upstream preprocess cannot run without it) | `train.include_errors` |
| `advanced.train.random_seed` | `11231` | whole number | random seed (training split and initialisation) | `train.random_seed` |
| `advanced.train.activation` | `"relu"` | `relu` / `tanh` / `sigmoid` | relu \| tanh \| sigmoid | `train.activation` |
| `advanced.reconstruct.ml_recon` | `true` | true / false | true = deterministic (MAP) reconstruction | `reconstruct.ml_recon` |
| `advanced.reconstruct.repeats` | `1` | whole number; >= 1 | > 1 samples the VAE (needs ml_recon: false) and adds SIG_recons | `reconstruct.repeats` |
| `advanced.blobs.sigdF_pct` | `95.0` | number; >= 0, <= 100 | percentile of sigma(dF) where difference weights fall off | `add_phases_and_blobs.sigdF_pct` |
| `advanced.blobs.absdF_pct` | `99.99` | number; >= 0, <= 100 | percentile of \|dF\| where difference weights fall off | `add_phases_and_blobs.absdF_pct` |
| `advanced.blobs.extrapolate_factors` | `[2, 4, 6, 8, 16]` | list of numbers | extrapolation factors written to the phased MTZs | `add_phases_and_blobs.extrapolate_factors` |
| `advanced.blobs.cutoff` | `3.5` | number; >= 0 | blob threshold (sigma) on the blurred \|difference map\| | `add_phases_and_blobs.cutoff` |
| `advanced.blobs.radius_in_A` | `4.0` | number; >= 0 | Gaussian blur radius (A) | `add_phases_and_blobs.radius_in_A` |
| `advanced.refine.eff` | `null` | path; or `null` | phenix parameter file (null = the packaged refine_drug.eff) |  |
| `advanced.refine.extra_args` | `[]` | list of text | extra command-line arguments for the refinement program |  |
| `advanced.refine.timeout_min` | `60` | whole number; >= 1 | give up on one dataset's refinement after this many minutes |  |
| `advanced.report.top_n` | `20` | whole number; >= 1 | number of top hits with maps and viewer entries |  |
| `advanced.report.maps` | `true` | true / false | write map files for the top hits |  |

## Checks across settings

Besides types and ranges, loading stops with an error (saying what to change) when:

- neither `models.apo` nor `models.per_dataset` is given;
- `phases.source` is `existing` without `phases.existing`, or `refine` without `phases.program`;
- `phases.source` is `input_mtz` or `existing` and `phases.columns.phwt` / `phdelwt` are empty;
- `advanced.train.train_fraction` is not strictly between 0 and 1 (upstream training crashes with
  an empty validation set);
- `advanced.train.n_hidden_layers` is not two positive whole numbers;
- `advanced.train.include_errors` is false (upstream preprocess cannot run without sigma(F));
- `advanced.reconstruct.repeats` > 1 with `ml_recon: true` (upstream crashes);
- `advanced.reindex.cc_min_dif` <= 0 (upstream writes no files);
- `advanced.blobs.extrapolate_factors` is empty.

`valdo check` adds checks that need the data (for example: at least one validation dataset
for the chosen `train_fraction`, and a warning below about 100 datasets).

## Environment variables

| variable | effect |
|---|---|
| `VALDO_NCPU` | overrides `compute.ncpu` for `valdo run` and `valdo report` (job scripts set it to the slots granted) |
| `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS` | set to `compute.ncpu` by `valdo run` and `valdo report` unless you set them |
| `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` | `''` hides GPUs: training then runs on the CPU |
